answer: Each agent must post a bond from a scarce, externally costly resource before it can submit work, and the protocol slashes that bond when a randomly audited claim fails. This makes identities cheap to create but costly to use: a sybil attacker must lock up more capital for every account and risks losing it on fabricated contributions. In an orchard, a lantern might mark a sampled claim; the delta between its promised and verified result determines the penalty. The defense raises attack cost, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker outright.
